ELIGIBLE: all three requirements are met. (1) Meta-analytic pooled estimate, not a single trial — k=32 with a pooled g = -0.30 and a reported CI [-0.39, -0.211]. (2) Objective cognitive performance outcome — primary domain is global cognition from administered performance tasks, not mood, fatigue, wellbeing, or subjective report. (3) Adults who are not a clinical/patient population — acute alcohol administration studies dose non-dependent healthy volunteers; this is an alcohol-challenge design, not an alcohol-use-disorder patient sample. Alcohol is also a genuine exogenous INTERVENTION (administered dose), not an endogenous biomarker that is merely measured, so the biomarker exclusion does not apply.

TIER = clean_MA: the pooled sample is healthy volunteers only. No MCI, dementia, or clinically diagnosed participants are folded into the estimate, and there is no indication of a mixed impaired/healthy pool, so the estimate is cleanly attributable to healthy adults.

CANDIDATE_ENHANCER = 0: this is the load-bearing call. Acute alcohol is studied exclusively as a physiological insult / intoxication challenge. Nobody ingests alcohol to improve memory, attention, executive function, or processing speed; it is not proposed, marketed, or used as a nootropic or performance supplement in any sense the ledger cares about. The signed effect is negative (-0.30) as expected for an impairer. Leaving this row unmarked in the primary enhancement stratum would let a trivial classifier ("alcohol is not a nootropic") score correctly and would inflate apparent predictive performance of any computational predictor being benchmarked. The row remains scientifically valuable as part of a separate IMPAIRMENT stratum — useful for testing whether a predictor recovers direction-of-effect — but it must be excluded from the primary healthy-adult enhancement analysis.

RED FLAGS: only acute_intoxication_state, which is descriptive of the exposure rather than a methodological defect. No other flags apply: the effect is modest and physiologically plausible (not implausible_effect_size), a CI is reported (not no_ci_reported), k=32 is a well-powered evidence base (not very_few_studies), and the population is explicitly recorded and internally consistent (not population_ambiguous). No duplicate signal was presented in the row.

ELIGIBLE: the row is a pooled meta-analytic estimate (k=11, SMD 0.46 [0.30, 0.63]), the outcome is an objective cognitive performance domain (memory, not mood/fatigue/subjective report), the exposure is a genuinely ingestible intervention (dietary anthocyanin supplementation — berry/anthocyanin extracts), and the pooled sample is adults that includes healthy participants rather than being a purely clinical/patient cohort. It is not an endogenous biomarker merely measured.

TIER = mixed_pop: the recorded population is explicitly healthy_mixed_with_impaired and the curator/verifier note states the pooled sample includes cognitively impaired participants alongside healthy adults. Per the conservative rule, an estimate pooled across healthy and MCI/cognitively-impaired participants cannot be cleanly attributed to healthy adults — impaired subgroups typically carry the larger response and can inflate the pooled effect. So clean_MA is not defensible here. It is not "contested": k=11 is a reasonable study count, a CI is reported and excludes the null, and g≈0.46 for a flavonoid memory outcome, while on the optimistic side, is not the implausible >1.0 small-study signature and there is no stated conflicting meta-analysis. I therefore did not add implausible_effect_size, no_ci_reported, or very_few_studies.

CANDIDATE_ENHANCER = 1: anthocyanins (blueberry/blackcurrant/cherry/aronia extracts, and the broader flavonoid class) are actively proposed, commercially marketed, and consumed as brain-health/nootropic supplements for memory and cognitive performance. This is an enhancement-direction exposure, not an impairment or physiological insult, so it belongs in the primary enhancement analysis stratum rather than the impairer stratum. The signed effect is positive and pro-cognitive, consistent with an enhancer hypothesis.

RED FLAG: population_ambiguous is the operative flag — downstream consumers must be able to exclude or sensitivity-test this row when the analysis requires healthy-adult-only attribution. No duplicate was indicated, and there is no acute intoxication state involved.

ELIGIBLE: ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) is an ingestible intervention a person can actually take, the row reports a pooled meta-analytic estimate (k=6, g=0.52, CI [0.27,0.78]) rather than a single trial, the outcome is a cognitive performance domain (global cognition, i.e. objective testing rather than mood/fatigue/wellbeing self-report), and the recorded sample is adults who are not a patient population. All three eligibility conditions are met.

CANDIDATE_ENHANCER = 1: ashwagandha is squarely an intentional nootropic/adaptogen — it is commercially marketed (KSM-66, Sensoril) and consumed specifically for stress resilience, memory and focus. It is the opposite of an impairment exposure like alcohol or sleep deprivation, so it belongs in the primary enhancement stratum, not the impairer stratum.

TIER = contested, not clean_MA and not mixed_pop. The population label as recorded ("healthy_mixed") is a healthy-adult label, so mixed_pop is not strictly forced by the recorded sample — but the tier decision is driven by a genuine methodological alarm rather than by population alone: (a) a pooled g=0.52 on GLOBAL cognition from only k=6 studies is a large effect for a botanical supplement and is the classic small-study / publication-bias signature — the ashwagandha trial base is dominated by small, single-site, frequently industry-sponsored studies; (b) the curator/verifier note records that the existing ledger already classifies ashwagandha as contested/mixed_pop on stressed samples, i.e. there are conflicting meta-analytic characterizations of this same compound, which is itself a "strongly conflicting meta-analyses" trigger; (c) the pooled base plausibly blends healthy volunteers with chronically-stressed and sub-clinical-anxiety enrollees, and several ashwagandha syntheses reach into MCI/clinical arms, so clean attribution to healthy adults is not defensible. Contested is the conservative call here because it captures both the population impurity and the effect-magnitude alarm; downgrading only to mixed_pop would understate the small-study risk.

RED FLAGS: implausible_effect_size (0.52 global-cognition effect from 6 small trials); very_few_studies (k=6, below any reasonable bias-detection threshold — Egger/funnel tests are uninformative under k=10); population_ambiguous ("healthy_mixed" plus stressed-sample provenance leaves the healthy-only claim unverified); duplicate_of_existing (the ledger already carries an ashwagandha row per the verifier note — this must be de-duplicated or explicitly superseded before it is scored, otherwise the compound is double-counted in predictor evaluation); other = the supporting quote "improved cognitive outcomes" is non-specific and does not name the instrument or domain, so the objective-performance criterion is satisfied by the recorded domain field rather than by the quote itself — the quote should be strengthened to an instrument-level extract before this row is used as ground truth.

RECOMMENDATION: retain as eligible and as a candidate enhancer, but tier it contested and resolve the duplicate against the existing ashwagandha entry before scoring.

ELIGIBLE: all three gates pass. (1) Meta-analytic — a pooled estimate with a CI across k=4 trials, not a single trial. (2) Objective cognitive outcome — global cognition performance, not mood/fatigue/wellbeing/subjective report. (3) Non-clinical adult sample — healthy older adults. The exposure is a genuine ingestible intervention (B-vitamin supplementation, i.e. folate/B12/B6 given as a supplement), not an endogenous biomarker merely measured, so the intervention criterion is satisfied.

TIER = clean_MA: the recorded population is healthy_older and the curator/verifier note states explicitly "healthy older adults." I flagged nothing for mixing. Caveat noted for downstream curation: the B-vitamin / homocysteine-lowering literature frequently pools cognitively normal elderly with MCI and dementia cohorts, so if a later audit shows this pooled sample admitted MCI or demented participants, this row should be downgraded to mixed_pop. On the record as given, there is no evidence of mixing, so clean_MA stands rather than a speculative downgrade.

NOT contested: the pooled effect is 0.00 with a tight symmetric CI [-0.05, 0.06]. That is the opposite of the small-study/publication-bias signature (implausibly large effect from few small trials), and I am aware of no strongly conflicting meta-analysis that would overturn a precise null here. A null with a narrow CI is an informative, well-behaved row.

CANDIDATE_ENHANCER = 1: this field asks whether the substance is PROPOSED/MARKETED/USED as a cognitive enhancer, not whether it works. B vitamins are among the most heavily marketed "brain health / memory support" supplements (B12, folate, B6 sold explicitly for cognition and brain aging, plus the homocysteine-lowering cognitive-protection hypothesis). Nobody takes B vitamins expecting to be impaired; this is not an insult or intoxication state. So it is squarely an enhancer candidate that happens to have failed. Rows like this are the most valuable content in an enhancement ledger — they are true negatives within the enhancer stratum, and they are exactly what stops a predictor from scoring well by trivially separating nootropics from impairers. Marking this 0 would be the error, because it would quietly remove a hard case.

RED FLAGS: "very_few_studies" — k=4 is thin, so the point estimate carries limited weight even though the CI is narrow; downstream weighting should reflect this. Not flagging no_ci_reported (CI present), not implausible_effect_size (effect is zero), not population_ambiguous (population explicitly stated by curator and verifier), not acute_intoxication_state, and no duplicate detected against the material provided — though a duplicate check against any other homocysteine-lowering/B-vitamin cognition row in the ledger is worth running at merge time, since that literature has overlapping trial pools.

Eligibility: all three criteria are met. (a) Meta-analytic pooled estimate, k=31 studies, not a single trial. (b) Objective cognitive performance outcome — attention, a core objective domain (not mood/fatigue/wellbeing/subjective report). (c) Adults who are not a clinical/patient population; the recorded population is healthy. Caffeine is an ingestible intervention a person can actually take, not an endogenous biomarker merely measured or correlated, so the intervention requirement is satisfied.

Tier: "healthy_mixed" here denotes heterogeneity WITHIN healthy adults (e.g., young + older, habitual + non-habitual users, varied dosing), not admixture of cognitively impaired/MCI/clinical participants. Nothing in the row indicates patient samples were pooled in, so the estimate remains cleanly attributable to healthy adults -> clean_MA. Note this is a label-semantics call: if downstream inspection of PMID:40335666 shows any MCI/dementia/patient arms were pooled, this must be downgraded to mixed_pop.

No contested tier: pooled g = +0.28 on attention is squarely in the expected range for caffeine (typical acute effects ~0.2-0.4 on vigilance/attention) and is supported by k=31, which is a healthy evidence base rather than the few-small-studies signature that produces small-study/publication-bias inflation. Neither implausible_effect_size nor very_few_studies applies. Direction and domain are consistent with the long-standing caffeine literature, so no strong meta-analytic conflict either.

candidate_enhancer = 1: caffeine is the canonical widely used, actively marketed cognitive/performance enhancer (coffee, energy drinks, pre-workout, nootropic stacks). It is taken deliberately to improve alertness and attention, and the pooled effect is signed pro-cognitive. This is an enhancement-stratum row, not an impairment/insult row, so it belongs in the primary enhancement analysis rather than the excluded-impairer stratum.

Red flags: (1) no_ci_reported — the pooled 0.28 arrives with no interval, so precision is unverifiable, the row cannot be inverse-variance weighted, and it cannot be tested for whether the effect excludes zero; recommend backfilling the CI/SE from the source before this row is used in any weighted scoring. (2) duplicate_of_existing — the curator flags this explicitly as an UPDATE of an existing caffeine row. That is not a defect in the evidence, but it is a ledger-integrity hazard: it must SUPERSEDE/merge into the existing caffeine record, never be appended alongside it, or caffeine gets double-counted and (being the single most-predictable positive in the ledger) would inflate apparent predictor performance. Deliberately not flagging population_ambiguous: "healthy_mixed" is a defined healthy label in this schema, not an unresolved clinical/healthy mixture.

ELIGIBILITY: passes all four requirements. (1) Meta-analytic pooled estimate with CI, not a single trial. (2) Objective cognitive performance outcome — pooled "global" cognitive/psychomotor performance under sleep deprivation, not mood/fatigue/sleepiness self-report (note: if on audit the pooled outcome turns out to be subjective sleepiness scales such as KSS/SSS rather than objective task performance, this row must be re-adjudicated as ineligible; the supporting quote "restored performance" reads as objective performance). (3) Population is healthy adults experimentally sleep-deprived — a transient induced state, not a clinical/patient population (no MCI, no sleep-disorder patients recorded). (4) Caffeine is a genuine ingestible intervention a person can take, not an endogenous biomarker.

TIER: clean_MA. The pooled sample contains no cognitively impaired, MCI, or clinical participants, so it does not meet the mixed_pop bar. It is also not "contested": d=0.68 with a tight CI [0.48, 0.88] is entirely plausible for caffeine countering a large sleep-deprivation-induced deficit — restoring a big deficit produces a big effect by construction — so there is no small-study/publication-bias signature and no known conflicting meta-analysis to invoke. I did NOT downgrade to contested merely because the effect is larger than typical rested-state caffeine effects (~0.2-0.3); the mechanism explains the magnitude.

CANDIDATE_ENHANCER = 1. The graded EXPOSURE here is caffeine, which is unambiguously proposed, marketed, and used as a cognitive enhancer / performance supplement. Sleep deprivation is the background condition of the sample, not the exposure being scored. The impairment-stratum rule (candidate_enhancer=0) targets rows where the thing administered is itself the insult — acute alcohol, dehydration, sedating daytime melatonin, sleep deprivation itself. Caffeine-under-SD is the opposite: an agent taken precisely to get sharper. Scoring this 0 would let a classifier fail on the single most canonical nootropic in the ledger.

FLAGS:
- duplicate_of_existing: curator explicitly notes a likely overlap with a plain "caffeine" row. This is the highest-priority flag — a rested-state caffeine MA and a sleep-deprived caffeine MA almost certainly share primary studies, so including both double-counts caffeine's evidence and, worse, inflates caffeine's apparent effect because the SD estimate (0.68) is roughly 2-3x the rested-state estimate. Recommend keeping ONE caffeine row in the primary enhancement analysis (the rested/healthy-baseline row) and holding this one in a sleep-deprivation stratum.
- population_ambiguous: this measures RESTORATION from an induced deficit toward baseline, not ENHANCEMENT above baseline. The ledger's question is enhancement in healthy adults; a deficit-repair effect is a different causal quantity and does not transfer to the rested-baseline case. The row is clean with respect to clinical contamination but is answering an adjacent question, so it should be labeled and analyzable separately.
- other: k (number of studies) is not reported, so heterogeneity, small-study bias, and the weight this row should carry cannot be assessed from the recorded fields. Not enough to make it "contested" on its own, but it blocks any power/precision weighting.
CI is reported, so no_ci_reported does not apply. No acute intoxication state (caffeine at cognitive doses is not an intoxicant here). Effect size is mechanistically plausible, so no implausible_effect_size.

ELIGIBILITY: All three requirements are met. (1) Meta-analytic pooled estimate across k=16 studies with a reported CI, not a single trial. (2) Outcome is objective cognitive performance pooled at the "global" cognition level (memory/attention/executive composites), not mood, anxiety, sleep quality, or subjective report — which matters here because most CBD literature is anxiolytic/sleep-focused, and this row is explicitly the cognitive-performance pool. (3) Population is adults who are not a clinical/patient group. (4) CBD is an ingestible exogenous intervention that a person actually takes — not an endogenous biomarker merely measured.

TIER: clean_MA. The recorded population "healthy_mixed" maps to the ledger's normalized healthy-adult categories (healthy adults of mixed age/sex), not to a mixture of healthy and impaired participants, and the curator/verifier note independently states "null effect in healthy adults." I therefore do not downgrade to mixed_pop. Caveat for downstream auditors: the broader CBD cognition literature frequently pools healthy volunteers with epilepsy, psychosis, and cannabis-use-disorder cohorts, so if the underlying k=16 set is later found to contain clinical arms, this row must be re-tiered to mixed_pop. As recorded, it is clean. Not "contested": the pooled effect is tiny (-0.048), the CI is narrow and straddles zero, k=16 is a respectable base, and there is no implausible-magnitude / few-small-studies signature.

CANDIDATE_ENHANCER = 1. CBD is a voluntarily consumed wellness/nootropic-market supplement, sold and promoted for "focus," "calm-alert" states, and neuroprotection, and it appears in commercial nootropic stacks. It is categorically unlike the impairment stratum (acute alcohol, dehydration, sleep deprivation, hangover, sedating daytime melatonin) — nobody is administered CBD as a physiological insult to degrade performance. The negative point estimate does NOT make it an impairer; the sign of the result is the thing the predictor is supposed to forecast, and coding an enhancer as an impairer because it failed would leak the outcome into the label and inflate apparent predictive performance. This is exactly the kind of row the ledger needs: a genuine, plausibly-marketed enhancer candidate that returns a well-powered null. Some primary CBD studies were framed as safety checks (does CBD impair like THC?), which is the only argument for 0, but the framing of individual trials does not change that the substance is proposed/marketed/used as an enhancer.

RED FLAGS: none. CI is reported, k=16 is not "very few," the effect size is small and plausible rather than implausible, no acute-intoxication framing (CBD is non-intoxicating), and population is unambiguous as recorded. No duplicate signaled.

ELIGIBILITY (true). All four gates pass: (a) the estimate is a pooled meta-analytic effect (k=3), not a single trial; (b) the primary domain is objective cognitive performance (global cognition test battery), not mood/fatigue/wellbeing — important because this source MA reports cognitive and mood outcomes separately and only the cognitive stream is being ingested here; (c) participants are adults; (d) Centella asiatica leaf extract is a genuinely ingestible, administrable intervention, not an endogenous biomarker merely measured. Eligibility is therefore independent of the precision problem — an imprecise or null pooled estimate is still a legitimate ground-truth row (it labels "no demonstrated enhancement").

TIER (mixed_pop, not clean_MA). The recorded label "healthy_mixed" in the ledger vocabulary connotes healthy adults of mixed age, but the underlying gotu kola meta-analysis (Puttarak et al., Sci Rep 2017; PMID 28878245) pools trials drawn from heterogeneous populations — healthy (elderly) volunteers alongside clinical samples including post-stroke vascular cognitive impairment and anxiety-disorder participants. With only k=3 contributing studies to this global-cognition pool, a single clinical trial can dominate the estimate, so the effect is not cleanly attributable to healthy adults. Per the instruction to prefer mixed_pop when a pool genuinely mixes impaired participants, this is mixed_pop. Downgrading is the safe error: the row stays in the ledger but is marked as not cleanly healthy-attributable.

NOT contested. I considered "contested" because 0.61 from 3 small herbal trials has the shape of a small-study signature. It does not qualify: the point estimate is moderate rather than implausibly large, the CI [-0.25, 1.48] is honestly reported and spans zero (so no inflated positive claim is being made), and I am not aware of a directly conflicting meta-analysis on this exposure. The defect here is imprecision/underpowering, which is captured by red flags rather than by the contested tier. Note the tier field allows only one value; population attribution is the more consequential problem, so it wins.

CANDIDATE_ENHANCER (1). Centella asiatica / gotu kola is a mainstream marketed nootropic and traditional "brain tonic," sold explicitly for memory and cognition and studied with pro-cognitive intent. It is unambiguously on the enhancer side of the enhancer/impairer split — nobody administers it as a physiological insult. This is the correct stratum for the primary enhancement analysis; it is NOT an impairment row, so it does not pose the trivial-classifier inflation risk.

RED FLAGS. very_few_studies: k=3 with a CI spanning zero — the estimate cannot distinguish a large benefit from a moderate harm, so any predictor scored against a positive label from this row would be scored against noise; downstream consumers should treat the label as null/indeterminate, not as a confirmed +0.61 enhancement. population_ambiguous: the "healthy_mixed" tag does not disclose whether clinical/post-stroke participants entered the k=3 pool, and the parent MA's inclusion set makes that plausible. Not flagging no_ci_reported (a CI is present) or implausible_effect_size (0.61 is within plausible range and is not statistically distinguishable from zero). No duplicate detected against the described row set.

SUGGESTED LABEL. Recording "mixed_healthy_and_clinical" rather than "healthy_mixed" so the mixed_pop tier and the population string agree; if a curator can confirm all three contributing trials enrolled non-clinical volunteers, this can be promoted to healthy_older / healthy_mixed and clean_MA.

(c) Adult samples that include healthy (non-patient) adults; not a purely clinical population. Per the conservative rule, an estimate that pools impaired/MCI participants cannot be cleanly attributed to healthy adults, so it is mixed_pop rather than clean_MA. I saw no evidence of strongly conflicting meta-analyses on this exposure that would rise to a methodological alarm.

CANDIDATE_ENHANCER = 1: cocoa flavanols are a canonical marketed/proposed nootropic-class supplement (explicitly named in the enhancer exemplars), studied and sold for cognitive benefit via cerebral blood flow / endothelial NO mechanisms. This is an enhancement row, not an impairment/insult row, so it belongs in the primary enhancement analysis and must NOT be excluded as an impairer stratum.

RED FLAGS: only population_ambiguous — the pooled sample straddles healthy and cognitively impaired participants, which is the sole reason for the mixed_pop tier. Not flagged: a CI is reported ([0.014, 0.434]), k=11 is not "very few studies", and the effect size is not implausible. Worth recording in reasoning rather than as a flag: the CI lower bound (0.014) is only marginally above zero, so the result is statistically fragile and should be treated as weak-positive evidence, and duplicate status against any other cocoa/flavanol row already in the ledger should be checked at merge time (no duplicate evidence available to me from this row alone).

INELIGIBLE on the intervention criterion, which is dispositive regardless of the other criteria. The curator/verifier notes state explicitly that this row captures an ENDOGENOUS hormone that was measured/correlated, not administered. Circulating cortisol level is the canonical example of a biomarker that is not something a person takes or receives, so it fails "an intervention that a person could actually take/receive." (Had this been an exogenous hydrocortisone-administration meta-analysis, the intervention test could have been met — but the row as recorded is the measured-biomarker version, and I adjudicate the row as recorded rather than re-verifying the citation.) The other two eligibility legs are not clearly satisfied either: the design is asserted to be meta-analytic but k is not reported, and the population is recorded as UNVERIFIED. The objective-cognitive-outcome leg is the only one that clearly passes (memory retrieval performance).

evidence_tier = "contested". Two independent alarms: (1) provenance is unauditable — no CI, no k, so the pooled estimate of -0.315 cannot be weighed at all and the classic small-study signature cannot be ruled in or out; (2) the underlying cortisol-memory literature is genuinely direction-conflicting by design phase — glucocorticoid exposure is repeatedly reported as IMPAIRING retrieval while ENHANCING consolidation, so a single signed pooled number is not attributable to "cortisol effect on memory" without the timing stratification. That is a real methodological alarm, not a bookkeeping gap. I did not choose "mixed_pop" because there is no positive evidence that the pooled sample includes MCI/clinical participants — "healthy_mixed" in this ledger's vocabulary reads as mixed age/sex healthy adults, and the actual defect is that the population was never verified, which I record as population_ambiguous rather than inventing clinical contamination. I did not choose "clean_MA" because the population is explicitly unverified and unverified is not clean.

candidate_enhancer = 0. Nobody takes cortisol to get smarter. Glucocorticoids are studied here as a stress-axis insult/physiological state, and the signed effect is negative (impairs memory retrieval). Marking this 1 would pad the enhancement stratum with a trivially-classifiable impairer and inflate apparent predictor performance — exactly the failure mode this field exists to prevent. It retains value only as an impairment-stratum row, and only if the provenance gaps are first closed.

red_flags: no_ci_reported (CI absent); very_few_studies (k not reported at all — flagged as an unknown-and-unauditable study count, not as a verified small k); population_ambiguous (population recorded UNVERIFIED); other = the exposure is an endogenous biomarker rather than an administered intervention, which is the actual eligibility killer, and the row's meta-analytic status is asserted but not evidenced by any reported k.

Recommended disposition: do not admit to the primary enhancement ledger. If the operator wants glucocorticoid coverage, re-curate from an exogenous cortisol/hydrocortisone ADMINISTRATION meta-analysis with reported k and CI, stratified by encoding/consolidation/retrieval phase, and file it in the impairment stratum unless a phase-specific pro-cognitive pooled estimate is what is being captured.

ELIGIBLE (true). All three gates are met: (a) it is a meta-analytic pooled estimate (k=33 studies, pooled g = -0.21 with a reported 95% CI), not a single trial; (b) the outcome is objective cognitive performance pooled to a global cognition domain (memory/attention/executive tasks), not mood, fatigue, or subjective report; (c) the pooled sample is non-clinical adults. It also clears the intervention bar: dehydration in these protocols is an EXPERIMENTALLY IMPOSED exposure (fluid restriction, exercise/heat-induced hypohydration) that is administered to participants, not an endogenous biomarker that is merely measured and correlated with cognition. That distinguishes it from, e.g., circulating cortisol levels, which would be ineligible.

evidence_tier = clean_MA. The recorded population is healthy_mixed, which denotes healthy adults spanning age/sex strata (young and older, athletes and sedentary), NOT a mixture of healthy and cognitively impaired/MCI/clinical participants. There is no indication that patient cohorts are pooled in, so the estimate is cleanly attributable to healthy adults. No "contested" signature either: the effect is small-to-modest (-0.21), it rests on a substantial evidence base (k=33), and the CI [-0.31, -0.11] is tight and excludes zero without being implausibly wide or implausibly large. This is the opposite of the few-small-studies/huge-effect publication-bias pattern.

candidate_enhancer = 0. This is the decisive call. Dehydration is a physiological insult, not something anyone ingests or induces in themselves to improve cognition. Nobody markets hypohydration as a nootropic; the direction of the recorded effect is negative by design and by intent (the supporting quote is literally "dehydration impaired cognition"). Scoring it as an enhancement candidate would let a trivial classifier win points on the obvious ("dehydration isn't a nootropic"), inflating apparent predictor performance. It should sit in the impairment stratum and be excluded from the primary healthy-adult enhancement analysis. Note that the inverse framing — rehydration/fluid supplementation as a performance aid — IS a marketed enhancement claim, but that is a different exposure than the one adjudicated here and must not be back-doored into this row by sign-flipping.

red_flags = ["other"]: the exposure is a physiological STATE (water restriction) rather than an ingestible or pharmacological agent, so it sits at the edge of the ledger's stated scope of "ingestible/pharmacological interventions." It qualifies as a receivable intervention and is retained, but downstream consumers should be able to filter state-exposure rows separately from agent rows. Not flagged: CI is reported; k=33 is far from very_few_studies; effect size is plausible; population is specified rather than ambiguous; acute_intoxication_state does not apply (dehydration is not an intoxicant). No duplicate detected in the material provided.

ELIGIBLE: the row is a pooled meta-analytic estimate (k=13, g=0.06, CI [-0.06, 0.18]), not a single trial; the outcome is objective cognitive performance pooled to a global cognition domain (not mood/fatigue/wellbeing/subjective report); and the exposure is a genuine ingestible intervention — inorganic dietary nitrate delivered as beetroot juice / nitrate supplementation — that a person can actually take, not an endogenous biomarker merely measured. Null direction is irrelevant to eligibility: the ledger needs signed effects including nulls, and a well-powered null is exactly the kind of row that keeps a predictor-scoring ground truth honest (a ledger of only positives would be unfalsifiable).

TIER = clean_MA: the recorded population is "healthy_mixed", which on its face denotes healthy adults spanning age strata (young/older, and typically mixed fitness/athlete vs sedentary in the nitrate literature), NOT a blend of healthy with MCI/dementia/clinical participants. The mixed_pop tier is reserved for pooled samples that genuinely contain cognitively impaired or patient participants, and nothing in the recorded row indicates that. I am flagging population_ambiguous rather than downgrading the tier, because the "_mixed" suffix is doing unlabeled work here: it does not state which axis is mixed, and nitrate/beetroot meta-analyses do sometimes fold in hypertensive or older cardiovascular-risk cohorts alongside healthy volunteers. If the curator can resolve the constituent samples and any cardiovascular-patient or MCI arms turn up, this row should be re-tiered to mixed_pop. Until then the conservative-but-accurate read is healthy-only with an explicit ambiguity flag.

CANDIDATE_ENHANCER = 1: this is the load-bearing call and it is unambiguous. Dietary nitrate/beetroot is actively marketed and consumed as a performance supplement, and the cognitive arm of that literature is explicitly enhancement-framed — the proposed mechanism is nitrate → nitrite → NO-mediated vasodilation raising cerebral blood flow to frontal/executive regions. Nobody administers beetroot juice to induce an impairment or as a physiological insult; it sits with caffeine, creatine and cocoa flavanols as a substance people take hoping to perform better. It therefore belongs in the primary enhancement stratum, not the impairment stratum.
